climate_pressure: Seasonal water and pasture dependence in a dryland livestock system.
documented_impact: War left Tekezze–Setit watering areas inaccessible and concentrated herds around Goluj and reintegration sites.
fcv_mediator: Conflict-related loss of transhumance/watering access and concentrated use of wells and cropland.
possible_consequence: Narrower seasonal coping options and localized livestock–farmer tensions were reported.
alternative_explanations: Borehole siting, herd numbers, settlement patterns and crop-residue management also shaped pressure.
uncertainty: Historical dryland coping mechanism from1999–2001 research, not measured climate-change impact, current violence or an evaluated adaptation project.
resilience_factors: Maintaining equitable water access and mobility options is relevant, without attributing pressures solely to displaced/returning people.
compact_statement: Near Goluj, border-war restrictions narrowed seasonal livestock water access and concentrated local resource pressures; findings are historical and exceptional.
